notes: Dev-split ABox contraction on a functional relation (has_father), paired with the revision people-replace-d001 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): it removes that revision's original fact, 'George W. Bush's father was George H. W. Bush' (same subject, relation and old object; statement = the revision's edit.original). It replaces the earlier removal of 'Will Smith is the father of Jaden Smith' (father_of), which was not paired. Every query routes through the removed fact and becomes 'does not know'; on a functional relation the cardinality question does too. Cardinality question: 'Was Henry Kissinger George W. Bush's father?' answers 'no' before, because a person has one father; after the removal the reason for 'no' is gone. Kissinger was chosen because that 'no' is not stated on its own (Dolma: 'Henry Kissinger is not the father' 0, 'Henry Kissinger was not the father' 0, 'Henry Kissinger was not George W. Bush's father' 0, 'Henry Kissinger was George W. Bush's father' 0, 'is not George W. Bush's father' 2, against 'Henry Kissinger' 325,917), he is a man born in 1923, old enough that age does not rule the question out, and he has no tie to the Bushes. As in the geography example, the cardinality question carries no derivability and no evidence entry, so its counts live here: Dolma counts as above, and the Kissinger article (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kissinger) says 'They had two children, Elizabeth and David, and divorced in 1964.' Residual risks, recorded: his Wikipedia article names his two children (Elizabeth and David), and his surname is not Bush, so a model may keep 'no' through biography or surnames, which is the 'no' kept by another route; any candidate father outside the Bush family has the surname route. Jimmy Carter, the revision's new value, was not used, so the contraction does not prime the revision's answer. Related near reads the removed fact through the inverse (has_father inverse:father_of), asked by role so George H. W. Bush's other children do not answer it. Related far is the binding through 'the 43rd president of the United States' (derivation none, task binding): its fact is stored (about 130 exact Dolma hits for 'father of the 43rd president', and the lead of George H. W. Bush's article), and it stays determinate because keeping the father under that role while dropping it under the name would contradict that George W. Bush is the 43rd president. The earlier second role binding (through Obama's predecessor, the revision's own derived query) was replaced after review, since it differed from related far only in whether the role-to-father link is stored; the two derived compositions now go through the removed fact by other stored facts about George H. W. Bush: his directorship of the Central Intelligence Agency and his vice presidency under Reagan. The revision's party composition was not reused: George W. Bush is himself a Republican, so a model could keep 'Republican' after a clean contraction by guessing from the son. Residual risks, recorded: the two names differ by one initial and share the surname, and Barbara Bush was George H. W. Bush's wife, so a model may rebuild the removed fact from the names or from the mother's marriage; that is the fact kept by another route, never a sign the removal worked. Unrelated near shares the subject (his mother); delete is exempt from Rule 7. Counts are exact-phrase Dolma counts from infini-gram, re-run on 2026-11-12 for this edit (the Kissinger, 'George W. Bush's father', 'father of the 43rd president', vice-president and Central Intelligence Agency counts all reproduced or newly run; the API answered normally). The counts copied from the revision (same fact, same evidence) are the ones shared with it. No claim here lacks a corpus count. Audit fix 2026-11-12: two models missed the 43rd-president check (answering Obama and Clinton), so the role is now given by the years of the presidency (2001 to 2009), which models hold better than an ordinal, and the vice-presidency check asks the common direction (Ronald Reagan's vice president). The related-far evidence is the two Wikipedia leads plus the 130 hits for the ordinal form; a direct count for the years form is missing (infini-gram was blocked).
